points.title: 童年与少年
points.description: 弗里达·卡罗出生于墨西哥城科约阿坎区的一个德裔墨西哥家庭。她6岁时患小儿麻痹症，导致右腿萎缩，这一经历影响了她的一生。尽管身体残疾，弗里达接受了良好的教育，进入国立预科学校，在那里她接触了墨西哥前卫艺术思想，并结识了后来成为她丈夫的著名壁画家迭戈·里维拉。这一时期，她开始对医学产生浓厚兴趣，并立志成为一名医生。
points.descriptionEn: Frida Kahlo was born in Coyoacán, Mexico City, to a German-Mexican family. At age 6, she contracted polio, which caused her right leg to be shorter and thinner than her left, a condition that would affect her throughout her life. Despite her physical challenges, Frida received a good education and attended the National Preparatory School, where she was exposed to avant-garde artistic ideas and met Diego Rivera, who would later become her husband. During this period, she developed a strong interest in medicine and aspired to become a doctor.

points.title: 车祸与艺术觉醒
points.description: 1925年，18岁的弗里达遭遇了一场严重的交通事故，导致她脊椎断裂、骨盆破裂等多处重伤。在长达数月的康复期间，她被迫卧床，开始绘画以打发时间。这次事故成为她人生的转折点，不仅带来了终身的健康问题，也意外地开启了她的艺术生涯。她最初的作品主要是自画像，记录自己的痛苦和康复过程。这一时期，她的艺术风格开始形成，融合了墨西哥民间艺术和超现实主义元素。
points.descriptionEn: In 1925, at age 18, Frida was involved in a serious bus accident that resulted in multiple injuries, including a broken spine and pelvis. During her long recovery period, confined to her bed, she began painting to pass the time. This accident became a turning point in her life, causing lifelong health issues but unexpectedly launching her artistic career. Her early works were primarily self-portraits, documenting her pain and recovery process. During this period, her artistic style began to form, blending Mexican folk art with surrealist elements.

points.title: 婚姻与早期创作
points.description: 1929年，弗里达与迭戈·里维拉结婚，开始了充满激情与痛苦的婚姻生活。这段关系充满了背叛与和解，两人于1939年离婚，后又于1940年复婚。在婚姻期间，弗里达的艺术创作逐渐成熟，她的作品开始受到关注。1938年，她在纽约举办了首次个人画展，获得评论界的好评。这一时期，她的作品主要关注自己的身体痛苦、身份认同和墨西哥文化，创作了《受伤的鹿》、《弗里达与迭戈·里维拉》等重要作品。她的健康问题持续恶化，多次接受手术。
points.descriptionEn: In 1929, Frida married Diego Rivera, beginning a passionate and tumultuous marriage marked by infidelities and reconciliations. They divorced in 1939 but remarried in 1940. During this marriage, Frida's artistic work matured and began to gain recognition. In 1938, she held her first solo exhibition in New York, receiving critical acclaim. During this period, her works primarily focused on her physical pain, identity, and Mexican culture, creating important pieces like 'The Wounded Deer' and 'Frida and Diego Rivera.' Her health problems continued to worsen, requiring multiple surgeries.

points.title: 国际声誉
points.description: 1939年，弗里达前往巴黎参加国际超现实主义展览，这是她首次离开墨西哥。在巴黎，她与毕加索、布勒东等著名艺术家交往，但她对超现实主义运动持保留态度，认为自己的作品源于真实经历而非梦境。尽管如此，她的艺术获得了欧洲艺术界的认可。这一时期，她创作了《两个弗里达》等代表作，深入探索了自我身份和情感复杂性。然而，她对巴黎艺术圈的商业化感到失望，最终选择返回墨西哥，坚持自己的艺术道路。
points.descriptionEn: In 1939, Frida traveled to Paris to participate in the International Surrealist Exhibition, her first time outside Mexico. In Paris, she mingled with famous artists like Picasso and Breton, but remained skeptical of the Surrealist movement, believing her work stemmed from real experiences rather than dreams. Despite this, her art gained recognition from the European art community. During this period, she created masterpieces like 'The Two Fridas,' deeply exploring self-identity and emotional complexity. However, she became disillusioned with the commercialism of the Paris art scene and eventually returned to Mexico, determined to follow her own artistic path.

points.title: 成熟期与政治活动
points.description: 1940年与迭戈复婚后，弗里达的艺术创作进入成熟期，作品更加自信和个人化。她积极参与墨西哥共产党和左翼政治活动，将政治元素融入艺术创作。1943年起，她在国立预科学校教授艺术，并成为墨西哥革命艺术运动的重要人物。尽管健康持续恶化，她坚持创作，并在1953年举办了墨西哥首次个人回顾展，亲自出席开幕式。这一时期，她创作了《破碎的柱子》、《根》等代表作，将个人痛苦与墨西哥历史、文化紧密结合，形成了独特的视觉语言。
points.descriptionEn: After remarrying Diego in 1940, Frida's artistic work entered a mature phase, becoming more confident and personal. She actively participated in Mexican Communist Party and leftist political activities, incorporating political elements into her art. From 1943, she taught art at the National Preparatory School and became an important figure in the Mexican revolutionary art movement. Despite worsening health, she continued to create and in 1953 held her first retrospective exhibition in Mexico, attending the opening ceremony in her bed. During this period, she created masterpieces like 'The Broken Column' and 'Roots,' combining personal pain with Mexican history and culture to form a unique visual language.

points.title: 最后岁月与遗产
points.description: 1953年至1954年是弗里达生命的最后阶段。她的健康状况急剧恶化，右腿被截肢，但她仍坚持创作。1954年7月，她在日记中写下最后记录，随后于7月13日去世，年仅47岁。她的遗体被展示在墨西哥城，被墨西哥人民视为民族英雄。弗里达去世后，她的作品逐渐被重新评价，从最初被视为迭戈·里维拉的附属，到后来被公认为20世纪最重要的艺术家之一。她的作品融合了墨西哥民间艺术、超现实主义和个人叙事，成为女性主义艺术、酷儿文化和后殖民研究的象征。
points.descriptionEn: 1953-1954 marked the final stage of Frida's life. Her health deteriorated rapidly, and her right leg was amputated due to gangrene, yet she continued to paint. In July 1954, she wrote her final diary entry before passing away on July 13 at the age of 47. Her body was displayed in Mexico City, where she was mourned by the Mexican people as a national hero. After her death, her work was re-evaluated, initially seen as secondary to Diego Rivera's, but later recognized as one of the most important artists of the 20th century. Her work, blending Mexican folk art, surrealism, and personal narrative, has become a symbol of feminist art, queer culture, and postcolonial studies.

supporter.zh: 弗里达·卡罗被视为一位勇敢无畏的艺术家和女性主义先驱。她通过艺术将个人痛苦转化为力量，打破了传统女性角色的束缚。她的自画像不仅是对身体痛苦的记录，更是对女性身份、政治立场和文化根源的深刻探索。弗里达的作品融合了墨西哥民间艺术与个人经历，创造了独特的视觉语言，影响了后世无数艺术家。她敢于直面自己的残疾和痛苦，并将其转化为艺术创作的源泉，展现了人类精神的不屈力量。
supporter.en: Frida Kahlo is celebrated as a fearless artist and feminist pioneer. She transformed personal pain into artistic power, breaking free from traditional female roles. Her self-portraits not only documented physical suffering but also explored female identity, political stance, and cultural roots with profound depth. Blending Mexican folk art with personal experience, she created a unique visual language that influenced countless artists. She dared to confront her disabilities and pain, turning them into sources of artistic creation, demonstrating the indomitable strength of the human spirit.

critic.zh: 批评者认为弗里达·卡罗的艺术成就被过度浪漫化，她的作品常被视为个人痛苦的简单记录而非真正的艺术创新。一些人指出她的政治立场有时显得肤浅，更多是姿态而非深度参与。此外，她的作品被批评为自我中心，缺乏对社会更广泛问题的关注。还有人质疑她与迭戈·里维拉的关系是否真正平等，认为她长期处于被支配地位。这些批评者认为，弗里达的传奇形象部分源于她悲剧性的人生故事，而非纯粹的艺术成就。
critic.en: Critics argue that Frida Kahlo's artistic achievements have been overly romanticized, with her work often seen as simple documentation of personal pain rather than true artistic innovation. Some suggest her political positions were sometimes superficial, more about posture than deep engagement. Additionally, her work has been criticized for being self-centered, lacking attention to broader social issues. Others question whether her relationship with Diego Rivera was truly equal, suggesting she remained in a subordinate position for much of her life. These critics contend that Frida's legendary status stems partly from her tragic life story rather than purely artistic merit.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，弗里达·卡罗已成为一个复杂的文化符号。她代表了女性主义艺术运动的重要先驱，其作品挑战了传统性别角色和艺术表达方式。她的自画像融合了个人叙事与墨西哥民族身份，成为后殖民研究的经典案例。在流行文化中，她被广泛视为反抗传统、拥抱多元身份的象征。她的生活故事和艺术风格影响了从时尚到电影等多个领域。然而，学术界也认识到，弗里达的形象经历了多次重构，从最初被视为迭戈的附属，到后来被独立评价，反映了艺术史评价标准的变化和文化政治的演变。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Frida Kahlo has become a complex cultural symbol. She represents an important pioneer of feminist art movements, challenging traditional gender roles and modes of artistic expression. Her self-portraits blend personal narrative with Mexican national identity, serving as classic case studies in postcolonial research. In popular culture, she is widely regarded as a symbol of rebellion against tradition and embrace of multiple identities. Her life story and artistic style have influenced fields ranging from fashion to film. Academia recognizes, however, that Frida's image has undergone multiple reconstructions—from initially being seen as Diego's附属 to later being evaluated independently—reflecting changes in art historical evaluation standards and the evolution of cultural politics.

self.zh: 我画自画像，因为我经常独处，因为我是我自己最了解的主题。
self.en: I paint self-portraits because I am so often alone, because I am the subject I know best.

others.zh: 弗里达·卡罗是一位伟大的画家，她用她的生命和痛苦创作了令人难以置信的艺术。
others.en: Frida Kahlo was a great painter who created incredible art from her life and suffering.
